root_cause.text: The block layer’s auto integrity buffer initialization in `bio_integrity_prep()` only zeroed the buffer when PI generation was disabled (`BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE`), leaving the extra opaque metadata bytes uninitialized whenever `metadata_size` was larger than `pi_tuple_size` even though PI was generated.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit says “the remainder ("opaque") of the metadata is left uninitialized” in the case where “PI is generated and the PI tuple size is nonzero, but the metadata size is larger than the PI tuple,” and the patch fixes this by changing the zeroing condition from `bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE` to `bi->metadata_size > bi->pi_tuple_size` in `block/bio-integrity-auto.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero integrity metadata buffers when metadata exceeds the PI tuple size instead of only when checksum type is none.
intent_record.what: In `bio_integrity_prep(struct bio *bio)`, the conditional that previously checked `bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE` was replaced with a check for `bi->metadata_size > bi->pi_tuple_size` before OR-ing `__GFP_ZERO` into `gfp`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, zero-initialization is now requested based on the metadata region being larger than the protection information tuple size, rather than based on the checksum type being none. This changes when allocated integrity metadata buffers are cleared, likely ensuring any extra metadata bytes beyond the PI tuple are zeroed and preventing stale data from being exposed or used.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it changes bio_integrity_prep() behavior to zero the integrity metadata buffer when metadata_size exceeds pi_tuple_size, fixing the uninitialized extra bytes that previously occurred when PI was generated.

candidates.rationale: This condition restricts zeroing of the integrity metadata buffer to the case where PI generation is disabled, which is the root cause of leaving extra metadata bytes uninitialized when metadata_size exceeds pi_tuple_size but checksums are still generated.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition limits zeroing of the integrity metadata buffer to the case where checksum generation is disabled, so when metadata_size is larger than pi_tuple_size and PI is still generated, the extra opaque metadata bytes remain uninitialized.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already contains the fix for the root cause. The vulnerable behavior was that auto integrity buffer initialization only zeroed the buffer when PI generation was disabled, leaving extra metadata bytes uninitialized when metadata_size exceeded pi_tuple_size even if PI was generated. In this snippet, write handling now does `if (bi->flags & BLK_INTEGRITY_NOGENERATE) { ... gfp |= __GFP_ZERO; } else if (bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE) gfp |= __GFP_ZERO;`, which preserves zeroing for the unchecked/host-buffer case and avoids the old overly narrow condition. Also, the code now conditionally skips generation only when appropriate with `if (bio_data_dir(bio) == WRITE && bip_should_check(&bid->bip)) blk_integrity_generate(bio);`, and `bi_offload_capable()` explicitly distinguishes when the controller can offload based on tuple size. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version and the fix is already included.
